issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period, but its own source_caveats records that the IRB protocol describes a four-year phased study with pilot collection begun November 2023 and still ongoing November 2024, and that a feasibility study ran 5 June to 28 July 2023. No start or end date is given for the window that produced version 3.1.0, so the collection period for the released data remains unresolved. The conflict is disclosed rather than concealed, which limits severity, but the temporal anchor a reuser needs is still absent.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record explicit start and end dates for the collection window represented in version 3.1.0, and state whether the 12 months are a subset of the wider four-year study period.

issues_detected.description: was_derived_from and parent_datasets are unpopulated even though preprocessing_strategies and raw_data_sources together document a complete derivation path from raw WAV waveforms to the released Parquet and TSV features. The lineage is fully recoverable from narrative text but is not expressed as typed, machine-readable provenance, so the entity-activity-agent relationships cannot be traversed programmatically.
issues_detected.recommendation: Express the feature-from-audio derivation as a typed was_derived_from relation linking the released feature tables to the controlled-access raw audio, naming b2aiprep as the generating agent.

issues_detected.description: variables enumerates only four fields (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames), all structural join or shape keys, while the record elsewhere describes phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata. Variable-level metadata is therefore far thinner than the data it documents, and a reuser cannot learn the phenotype schema from this record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Extend variables to cover the phenotype table columns, or reference the published JSON data dictionaries as the authoritative variable-level description.

issues_detected.description: Feature-extraction software is named without version pins: openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, sparc and ppgs carry no version, and 'OpenAI Whisper Large' names a model size rather than a release (large-v1, v2 and v3 differ materially). Because openSMILE feature sets and Whisper transcription outputs differ across releases, the extraction pipeline is not exactly reproducible from this record, despite otherwise exemplary parameter documentation.
issues_detected.recommendation: Pin version numbers for openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, sparc and ppgs, and name the exact Whisper checkpoint used.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is set to false in absolute terms, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that k-anonymisation with k of 2 or more is not achieved and that re-identification by voice cannot be entirely excluded. The two are reconcilable because raw audio is excluded from the registered-access release, but the unqualified false flag understates the residual risk carried by the released phenotype tables, which are explicitly not k-anonymous.
issues_detected.recommendation: Qualify the flag to state that direct identifiers are absent while residual re-identification risk persists because k-anonymity is not achieved.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts is unpopulated. The substance of a data protection impact assessment is present but dispersed across regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, administrative, physical and technical safeguards, five-business-day breach reporting) and participant_privacy (two-tier access justified by re-identification risk). No consolidated DPIA is recorded under the field the rubric names.
issues_detected.recommendation: Consolidate the existing safeguard, breach-reporting and risk material into an explicit data_protection_impacts entry.

issues_detected.description: keywords contains only four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). None of the five disease cohort categories enumerated in description and subpopulations appears as a keyword, and no disease vocabulary term is present, so a search for a specific condition such as dysphonia or Parkinson disease will not surface this record. The B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE CURIEs present on instances are program-internal identifiers rather than discovery vocabulary.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add disease-cohort and modality keywords, and where possible ICD-10 or MeSH terms matching the diagnostic labels already described in labeling_strategies.

issues_detected.description: publisher is not populated as a field, although PhysioNet is unambiguously identified as the publishing platform in citation, maintainers, data_governance.stewardship_roles and the page URL. Questions 6 and 13 both reference publisher for hosting-platform identification, which must here be inferred rather than read.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate publisher with PhysioNet to make the hosting platform directly machine-readable.

issues_detected.description: source_caveats records that grant identifier renderings vary across the source bundle, including the malformed string '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' in a documentation footer, alongside OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 3OT2OD032720-01S3 and 1OT2OD032720-01. The record selects well-formed NIH renderings for the funders field, so the defect lies in the sources rather than in this datasheet, and the disclosure is a documentation strength.
issues_detected.recommendation: No correction needed to funders; optionally note which rendering is the authoritative core project number for citation purposes.

issues_detected.description: Instance counts differ across sources: the project documentation describes approximately 61,937 voice-derived recordings from 833 adult participants, whereas the PhysioNet release pages give per-feature counts (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files) and no single recording total. instances records the participant count of 833 but leaves the recording-level instance without a count. The discrepancy is disclosed and adjudicated in favour of the higher-ranked source.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record per-feature recording counts on the audio recording instance so the released volume is readable without consulting source_caveats.

issues_detected.description: content_warnings.source_caveats records a conflict over whether free-speech transcriptions are included in the release: the project documentation says they are, the PhysioNet release notes say transcripts of free speech audio and spectrogram-family features derived from free speech were removed. The record resolves this to the PhysioNet statement and adjusts the warning accordingly, which is correct adjudication of a genuine source conflict.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required; the resolution is sound and the reasoning is recorded.

issues_detected.description: license_and_use_terms names a custom licence, the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, which carries no SPDX identifier. The terms are described at length and are unambiguous in substance, but automated licence reasoning over this record cannot resolve the licence to a known identifier, unlike the MIT and Apache-2.0 licences correctly attached to external_resources.
issues_detected.recommendation: Publish a stable URI for the Registered Access License text and reference it alongside the human-readable terms.

semantic_insights: The description is substantive at well over 2,000 characters and carries specific, checkable facts: 833 participants, five North American sites, five named disease cohort categories plus controls, and an enumerated list of released feature types.

The PhysioNet DataCite prefix 10.13026 is used correctly and consistently across six version-specific DOIs, and the record correctly distinguishes the version-specific DOI (10.13026/8xbn-nq66, matching version 3.1.0) from the version-agnostic latest-version DOI (10.13026/37yb-1t42) recorded separately in version_access.latest_version_doi.
The Health Data Nexus prefix 10.57764 and the Zenodo prefix 10.5281 are each applied to the correct resource, showing the registrar distinctions were understood rather than homogenised.

The NIH grant OT2OD032720 follows the expected activity-code, institute, serial pattern (OT2 / OD / 032720), and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 is a well-formed full award number with support year and supplement segments.
RRID:SCR_007345 is well-formed and is correctly used to identify the hosting resource within the citation rather than being misapplied as an identifier for the dataset itself.

HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification supplemented by indirect-identifier removal, sensitive-field removal and wholesale exclusion of raw audio is the semantically appropriate method for voice data, where the waveform is itself a biometric identifier; the record reasons explicitly to that conclusion rather than asserting compliance.

The two-tier access model is internally coherent: registered access for derived features whose re-identification risk is low, controlled access via DACO for raw audio whose risk is high, with the ethics working group memorandum cited as the justification for the split.

Preprocessing parameters are specific enough to reproduce the pipeline structure: 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 MFCCs and 60-bin Mel spectrograms, articulatory traces at 50 Hz, phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 acoustic units at 100 Hz.

known_biases uses BiasTypeEnum-style categorical values (representation_bias, selection_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) rather than free text, and the measurement_bias entry correctly identifies a site-device-cohort confound in which disease group is entangled with recording configuration.

The record makes several honest negative disclosures that a less careful datasheet would omit: k-anonymity with k of 2 or more is not achieved, Whisper transcripts were generated by an off-the-shelf model that has not been audited for correctness, a single labeler provided each diagnostic label, and the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment scores sustainability at 50 percent with named unmet criteria.

source_caveats is used systematically as an adjudication mechanism, recording conflicts in participant counts, enrollment targets, consortium size, grant renderings, investigator name spellings and free-speech transcript inclusion, and stating which source was preferred and why in each case.

Temporal ordering across the release history is internally consistent: version 1.0 in November 2024 through version 3.1.0 on 1 May 2026, matching the issued date of 2026-05-01 and the declared version 3.1.0.

Access governance is described end to end, from PhysioNet registration and identity confirmation through the Registered Access Agreement, to the Data Access Request Form, DACO review and institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement for raw audio, with a named contact address.

The absence of a direct download URL is explained rather than silently left blank: the record states that PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing so the landing page is the access URL, which is more useful than an empty field.

Vulnerable-population documentation is unusually complete, covering cognitive impairment, dementia, psychiatric conditions and paediatric participants, with comprehension-confirmation during consent, single-guardian permission justified by minimal risk, and an age threshold below which assent is not sought.

questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated (id, title, description, keywords, license, doi, page, creators, purposes, instances, resources, parent_datasets, variables, confidentiality_level).
questions.score_label: Approximately 86% of mandatory fields populated, between the 70% and 90% bands
questions.evidence: Populated: id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (>2,000 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms (data_use_permission 'general_research_use' plus detailed license_terms); doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (15 principal investigators, each with an affiliation); purposes (5); instances (2, research participant counts 833 and audio recording); variables (4); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Unpopulated: resources, parent_datasets. That is 12 of 14 named fields.
questions.quality_note: Twelve of fourteen named fields are populated and nearly all carry substantive rather than token content, placing the record at roughly 86% and short of the 90% threshold for 5. The two absent fields are the hierarchical-structure pair; related_datasets partly compensates by typing the pediatric and version-1.0 relationships, but it is not the same construct as parent_datasets.
questions.semantic_analysis: Beyond bare presence, the populated fields are semantically appropriate to their names: confidentiality_level 'restricted' matches the registered-and-controlled access model described in data_governance, and the id is the version-specific DOI matching the declared version 3.1.0 rather than the latest-version DOI. One field passes presence but is semantically thin: variables lists only four structural join and shape keys for a dataset whose phenotype tables span demographics, diagnosis, enrolment and questionnaires. This was recorded as a completeness issue rather than deducted twice here.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields (description, purposes) have meaningful content length.
questions.score_label: >200 chars
questions.evidence: description runs to well over 2,000 characters, covering cohort composition, recruitment setting, protocol, version 3.1.0 participant count of 833, the released feature types, the exclusion of raw audio from public release, and the consortium's AI-readiness self-assessment percentages. purposes contains five entries, each itself over 200 characters, for example: 'To generate a large, multi-institutional, ethically sourced and diverse voice, speech, cough and respiratory sound dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers, in order to fuel voice AI research.'
questions.quality_note: Both narrative fields far exceed the 200-character threshold for the top band, and the length is carrying information rather than padding.
questions.semantic_analysis: Length is matched by density. The description states checkable particulars (833 participants, five sites, named feature types, named file formats) instead of generic framing, and the five purposes are distinct from one another rather than restatements, covering dataset generation, model development, clinical integration, standards creation and infrastructure. addressing_gaps and tasks extend the narrative further without duplicating it.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords provided to describe dataset topic coverage.
questions.score_label: 3-7 keywords
questions.evidence: keywords: 'health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice' - four unique terms. Supplementary topic coding exists on instances (data_topic 'B2AI_TOPIC:25', 'B2AI_TOPIC:36', data_substrate 'B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30') and labeling_strategies references ICD-10 codes, but no disease or modality term appears in the keywords field itself.
questions.quality_note: Four keywords sits squarely in the 3-7 band. The rubric permits keywords to be supplemented by condition lists and external ontology references, and that supplementation was checked, but what exists is program-internal CURIEs and a passing mention of ICD-10 rather than an enumerated condition vocabulary, which is not enough to lift the record toward the 8-or-more band.
questions.semantic_analysis: The gap is a discoverability one and is visible as an internal mismatch: description and subpopulations enumerate five disease cohort categories (voice, neurological and neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, respiratory, pediatric voice and speech), none of which is reachable through the keywords. Three of the four terms are also very broad ('health', 'biomarkers', 'voice') and one is a program name, so the keyword set does little to distinguish this dataset from any other Bridge2AI voice record.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of distribution formats and file type diversity.
questions.score_label: >3 file types
questions.evidence: distribution_formats contains three entries spanning four distinct file types: 'Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format, holding the dense derived audio features'; 'Tab-separated values with accompanying JSON data dictionaries'; and 'WAV audio files with accompanying JSON sidecars, organized per the Brain Imaging Data Structure'. Unique types: Parquet, TSV, JSON, WAV. Per-feature file counts appear in source_caveats (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files).
questions.quality_note: Four unique file types clears the >3 threshold for the top band, and each format entry states what it holds rather than only naming an extension, so the variety is interpretable rather than nominal.
questions.semantic_analysis: The variety genuinely reflects multi-modality as indicated in description and purposes: dense numeric features in a columnar format, tabular phenotype data in TSV with JSON data dictionaries, and audio in WAV under BIDS. Format choice matches content type in each case, which is the semantic test rather than the count alone. Two enumeration weaknesses were noted but did not move the score off the band: file_collections and total_file_count are unpopulated, and the file counts that do exist sit in a source_caveats narrative rather than a count field.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or instance count metadata.
questions.score_label: Pass - numeric instance count found
questions.evidence: instances[0] gives instance_type 'research participant' with counts 833. description repeats 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants across five North American sites'. splits is populated ('No recommended training, validation or test splits are provided'), subpopulations contains two entries, and source_caveats supplies per-feature file counts of 32,522, 29,278 and 29,289.
questions.quality_note: Passes on an explicit numeric instance count that is corroborated in two places. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent, so byte volume must be estimated from counts, but the pass criterion is satisfied by instance count alone.
questions.semantic_analysis: The count of 833 is internally consistent between instances and description and matches the PhysioNet figure the record says it preferred. The audio recording instance carries no count, and the documentation-versus-PhysioNet discrepancy over total recordings (approximately 61,937 against per-feature totals) is disclosed in source_caveats rather than silently reconciled, which is the correct handling of a conflict even though it leaves the recording-level volume imprecise.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs, and hosting platform identification.
questions.score_label: Pass - multiple persistent identifiers found
questions.evidence: doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; citation contains 'RRID:SCR_007345' and 'https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; version_access.latest_version_doi 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42' plus version-specific DOIs 10.13026/249v-w155 and 10.13026/k81f-qr68; related_datasets carry doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 and doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84.
questions.quality_note: Passes comfortably. Several independent persistent identifiers are present and the hosting platform is identifiable as PhysioNet from the page URL, the citation, maintainers and data_governance.stewardship_roles.
questions.semantic_analysis: The identifiers are not merely present but correctly differentiated: the version-specific DOI is used as the record's own identity while the version-agnostic DOI is filed separately under version_access, which is the correct semantics for a versioned PhysioNet deposit. The RRID is well-formed and identifies the hosting resource inside the citation rather than being misused as a dataset identifier. The one weakness is that publisher is not populated as a field, so platform identification must be inferred; this was recorded as a low-severity consistency issue and does not defeat the pass criterion.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, creator affiliations, and institutional sponsors.
questions.score_label: Funders with grants + creators with affiliations
questions.evidence: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund' with grants 'OT2OD032720' and '3OT2OD032720-01S1', and notes 'The funded project period runs from 1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026, with the project administered by the University of South Florida.' creators lists 15 principal investigators each with a named affiliation, for example Yael Bensoussan (USF Health Morsani College of Medicine, University of South Florida), Olivier Elemento (Englander Institute for Precision Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine), Satrajit Ghosh (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Jennifer Siu (The Hospital for Sick Children).
questions.quality_note: Both halves of the top band are satisfied: funders carry actual award numbers rather than an agency name alone, and every creator carries an institutional affiliation. The funding entry additionally supplies the project period and the administering institution, which exceeds what the band requires.
questions.semantic_analysis: Grant format validation passes: OT2OD032720 follows the NIH activity-code, institute, serial pattern (OT2 / OD / 032720), consistent with an NIH Common Fund Other Transaction award, and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 is a well-formed full award number with support-year and supplement segments. The funding is also semantically aligned with purposes, which describe exactly the kind of consortium infrastructure and standards work an OT2 Common Fund award supports. source_caveats discloses that the sources render the grant identifier five different ways including a malformed '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2', and the record selected well-formed renderings, so the variance is a source defect that has been correctly filtered rather than propagated.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition established from fields outside Q8, per the anti-circular rule: description (Q1/Q2) states 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada' and 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants'; keywords (Q3) includes 'health'; collection_mechanisms (Q12) describes 'the custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet, which hosts the acoustic task protocol, demographic surveys' administered to participants in clinic.
questions.description: Comprehensive ethics coverage including IRB approval, deidentification, privacy protections, informed consent, participant compensation, vulnerable population safeguards, and re-identification risk analysis.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive - all human subjects protections and data protection impacts documented
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews names three reviewing bodies (USF IRB, Research Ethics Board at The Hospital for Sick Children, and the Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group which 'identified the sensitive fields removed from the release and produced a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for controlled access to raw voice data samples'). human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval, ethics_review_board naming the single-IRB arrangement and separate Canadian REB approvals, regulatory_compliance citing HIPAA and NIH STRIDES hosting, special_populations. is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers...', with a full identifiers_removed enumeration and deidentification_details ('Dates are rebased and replaced by integers... K-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved'). participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk, data_linkage. participant_compensation: 40 USD under 90 minutes, 80 USD over, maximum 120 USD. at_risk_populations: special_protections, guardian_consent, assent_procedures. informed_consent: consent_type, consent_scope, consent_documentation, withdrawal_mechanism. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant 'compliant'; other_compliance records a Certificate of Confidentiality and five-business-day breach reporting.
questions.quality_note: Every protection area named by the rubric is covered, most of them in operational detail rather than assertion - compensation with amounts and caps, consent with four alternative modalities and a documented withdrawal rule, assent with an age threshold. Re-identification risk is analysed explicitly and negatively, which is the hardest part of this question to earn honestly.
questions.semantic_analysis: Cross-field logic passes: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a documented method and by listed participant_privacy protections. The method is appropriate to the data type, which is the substantive test - Safe Harbor alone would be insufficient for voice because the waveform is itself biometric, and the record reasons to exactly that conclusion by excluding raw audio from the release and routing it through DACO. Two gaps were weighed and did not reduce the score: data_protection_impacts is unpopulated, but its substance (safeguards, breach reporting, Certificate of Confidentiality, risk-justified access tiering) is documented under regulatory_restrictions and participant_privacy, and the instruction is to score content rather than field presence; and governance_committee_contact is unpopulated while data_governance supplies the committee name and the DACO@b2ai-voice.org address. The unqualified is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present false sits in mild tension with the acknowledged failure to reach k of 2 and was recorded as a low-severity issue.

questions.name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions, and confidentiality level are clearly defined.
questions.score_label: License + restrictions + confidentiality classification + governance contact
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission 'general_research_use' with license_terms describing the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, the requirement that credentialed users sign the Registered Access Agreement, permission to duplicate as reasonably required, prohibition on sale, non-obstruction licensing policy, the Fort Lauderdale Agreement, and 'There are no fees associated with these restrictions.' ip_restrictions sets out copyright and database rights, non-transfer of IP, and downstream rights conditional on non-obstructive licensing. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance covering the Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguards and five-business-day breach reporting. data_governance: committee_name 'Bridge2AI-Voice Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)', a full access_review_process, accountable_organization 'University of South Florida', and stewardship_roles with the DACO@b2ai-voice.org contact.
questions.quality_note: All four components of the top band are present and each is specified rather than gestured at. The access review process distinguishes the registered tier from the controlled tier and states that collaborators at other organisations must apply independently, which is the kind of operational detail that determines whether a reuser can actually obtain the data.
questions.semantic_analysis: The governance claims are mutually plausible and correctly scaled. confidentiality_level 'restricted' is consistent with a registered-plus-controlled model rather than overstated as open or understated as internal-only; hipaa_compliant 'compliant' is supported by the documented Safe Harbor method rather than asserted bare; the Certificate of Confidentiality noted under other_compliance is consistent with confidential_elements.source_caveats, which records the same certificate against a headline statement that no privileged data are held. Multi-jurisdiction coverage is genuine, with the USF single IRB for United States sites and separate Canadian REB approvals recorded under human_subject_research. The only weakness is that the licence is custom and carries no resolvable identifier, recorded as a low-severity semantic issue.

questions.name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition established from fields outside Q10's scoring core: distribution_formats is populated with three format entries carrying access_urls, page resolves to 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/', third_party_sharing.is_shared is true, and license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission 'general_research_use' permits reuse by approved researchers.
questions.description: Presence of standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance, cross-platform dataset linkages with typed relationships, and dataset integration capability.
questions.score_label: Standard formats + schema/ontology compliance + integration capability
questions.evidence: Standard formats: Apache Parquet, tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries, WAV with JSON sidecars. Schema and standard conformance: conforms_to 'Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0', conforms_to_standard ['BIDS'], conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema', conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Ontology terms: instances carry data_topic 'B2AI_TOPIC:25' and 'B2AI_TOPIC:36' and data_substrate 'B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30'; labeling_strategies states 'Labels follow the Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes'. Integration keys: variables document participant_id as 'present in every Parquet feature file and used to join the phenotype tables' and session_id as the session key. related_datasets gives two typed relationships, 'is_supplemented_by' to doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 and 'is_new_version_of' to doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. external_resources includes FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker and the b2aiprep and senselab repositories.
questions.quality_note: Every component of the top band is satisfied. Formats are open and standard, conformance is declared against a named versioned standard rather than a bare label, and integration is concretely supported by a documented join key rather than merely asserted.
questions.semantic_analysis: The conformance claims are semantically coherent with the content: BIDS v1.9.0 is a domain-appropriate organising standard for the audio, and preprocessing_strategies confirms the conversion was actually performed, including the two-step route by which pediatric ReproSchema data were transformed into REDCap format and then to BIDS. The LinkML schema URI is well-formed and w3id-based, so schema conformance is machine-resolvable. Cross-platform linkage spans PhysioNet, Synapse, Health Data Nexus and Zenodo, each with a correctly formed identifier for its registrar. The named ICD-10 and FHIR alignments give semantic interoperability beyond format interoperability. The chief residual limitation is the thin variables list, which weakens field-level harmonisation; it is recorded as a separate completeness issue and was not deducted here because the integration keys the question asks about are documented.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: Software-output condition established from fields outside Q11, per the anti-circular rule: external_resources (Q14) references code repositories, namely 'sensein/b2aiprep, the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset... at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep', 'sensein/senselab... at https://github.com/sensein/senselab', and 'eipm/bridge2ai-redcap... at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap'. extension_mechanism.contribution_url also resolves to https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep.
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing, cleaning, and labeling strategies with software tools used in data preparation, including annotation quality, imputation, and missing data documentation.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive strategies with URLs, but software versions largely unpinned
questions.evidence: preprocessing_strategies gives eight entries with explicit parameters: conversion to monaural and resampling 'to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter'; STFT spectrograms with 'a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT'; 'Sixty Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients and 60-bin Mel spectrograms'; articulatory features via 'the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package... all gathered at 50 Hz'; 'Acoustic features were extracted with openSMILE, and phonetic and prosodic features... with Parselmouth and Praat'; posteriorgrams 'over 40 acoustic units of speech at 100 Hz... with the ppgs package'; transcriptions via 'OpenAI's Whisper Large model'; BIDS v1.9.0 conversion. cleaning_strategies documents an audit protocol with missingness tables, outlier checks, schema checks and audio quality-control metrics. labeling_strategies gives annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol and data_annotation_platform. machine_annotation_tools names Whisper Large with tool_accuracy: 'off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'. missing_data_documentation covers causes, patterns and handling ('no imputation is applied').
questions.quality_note: Far beyond the 3-band of one strategy listed: four distinct strategy families are documented with named tools and reproducible numeric parameters, and the generating library is linked. Held one point below the top band because the top band names software versions as well as URLs, and versions are largely absent.
questions.semantic_analysis: The tools named are correct and correctly attributed to their functions - openSMILE for static acoustic descriptors, Parselmouth as the Python interface to Praat for f0, formants and voice quality, sparc for articulatory kinematics, ppgs for phonetic posteriorgrams, Whisper for transcription. Terminology is used accurately throughout. imputation_protocols is unpopulated but that is a documented decision rather than an omission, since missing_data_documentation states a missingness table is produced and no imputation applied, which is the more informative answer. The deduction rests on a genuine reproducibility consequence rather than field absence: openSMILE feature sets differ materially between releases and 'Whisper Large' names a model size spanning large-v1, v2 and v3 with different transcription behaviour, so the pipeline cannot be reproduced exactly from this record. Honest disclosure that the transcription model was never audited is a countervailing strength and is why the score remains at 4 rather than 3.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.applicability_evidence: Both limbs met from fields outside this question's scoring core. Collection identified: acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors and collection_timeframes are all populated. Datasets shared: distribution_formats populated with access_urls, page resolves to the PhysioNet landing page, and third_party_sharing.is_shared is true.
questions.description: Description completeness of data collection mechanisms, acquisition methods, data collectors, and collection timeframes.
questions.score_label: Full collection protocol with methods, collectors, and timeframes
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods gives four typed entries - was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified and was_inferred_derived - each with details, including 'Clinical diagnoses were verified by clinicians reviewing audio and/or imaging data, consulting electronic health records, or examining medication prescriptions, in accordance with established gold standards for each disease cohort.' collection_mechanisms gives four entries down to hardware: 'iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; a head-mounted headset with microphone was used where possible, though the microphone could sit at slightly different distances between recordings.' data_collectors gives three entries distinguishing research teams, clinicians providing gold-standard assessment, and hospital staff. collection_timeframes: 'The data were collected over a period of 12 months' with a source_caveats note. raw_data_sources gives two entries with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. direct_collection and sampling_strategies add non-probability sampling, cohort-based recruitment and why_not_representative.
questions.quality_note: All three components named by the top band are present, and methods and collectors are documented to an unusually operational level - recording hardware by model and generation, the division of labour between research staff and clinicians, and the distinct adult and pediatric collection applications.
questions.semantic_analysis: The acquisition typing is semantically correct: directly observed for the recordings, self-reported for questionnaires, validated for diagnoses, and inferred for the released features, which correctly classifies the derived features as inference rather than observation. The mechanisms are internally consistent with preprocessing_strategies, which describes converting ReproSchema and REDCap exports to BIDS exactly as the mechanisms describe them being captured. The one weak limb is the timeframe: 12 months is stated without start or end dates and its own source_caveats flags a conflict with a four-year IRB protocol. That was recorded as the single failed consistency check. It did not reduce the score because the record discloses and reasons about the conflict rather than asserting a false precision, and because the methods, collectors and raw-source documentation exceed the top band by a clear margin.

questions.name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
questions.applicability_evidence: Both limbs met from fields outside this question's scoring core. Collection identified: acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms and data_collectors are populated (Q12). Datasets shared: distribution_formats populated with access_urls, page resolves to the PhysioNet landing page, third_party_sharing.is_shared is true.
questions.description: Presence of version information, version access methods, errata, update plans, release notes with dates, and data sustainability indicators.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive versioning + full sustainability documentation
questions.evidence: version '3.1.0'. version_access: versions_available covering version 1.0 on Health Data Nexus and 1.1 through 3.1.0 on PhysioNet, latest_version_doi 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42', and version_details giving per-version DOIs and the policy that 'older versions of the dataset continue to be supported, hosted and made available to researchers'. errata gives three substantive entries including 'Version 3.1.0 fixed broken Parquet files carried in the version 3.0.0 release, and back-filled and updated validated diagnosis information across conditions'. updates: frequency 'Semi-annual (twice a year)', update_details with notification via platform news items, and 'Each version of the dataset has a unique DOI.' maintainers gives three entries with roles (government_agency, academic_institution). distribution_dates lists six dated releases from late November 2024 to 1 May 2026. retention_limit and extension_mechanism with contribution_url are also populated.
questions.quality_note: Versioning is comprehensive and all four sustainability indicators are evidenced: persistent identifiers throughout, a long-term governance plan in data_governance and retention_limit, a domain-appropriate repository in PhysioNet for biomedical data, and institutional commitment through NIH programme funding, MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology hosting and T-CAIREM hosting of the earlier release.
questions.semantic_analysis: Versioning semantics are handled correctly, which is the discriminating test here: the record's own identifier is the version-specific DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 matching the declared version 3.1.0, while the version-agnostic 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is filed under latest_version_doi, and the Health Data Nexus release correctly carries a different registrar prefix (10.57764). Release chronology is internally consistent and matches issued 2026-05-01. The errata are genuine content changes rather than boilerplate, and one of them documents a data defect (broken Parquet files) rather than only additions, which is a meaningful integrity disclosure. The record also reproduces the consortium's own self-assessment scoring sustainability at 50 percent and names the unmet criteria; this is a limitation of the underlying programme rather than of the documentation, and the documentation of sustainability here is complete. publisher being unpopulated is a minor machine-readability gap recorded separately.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.description: Presence of formal citations or external resources with DOI-linked references.
questions.score_label: At least two distinct references documented and a formal dataset citation present
questions.evidence: citation is a complete formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, authors and publishing organisation: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. external_resources supplies six distinct references: eipm/bridge2ai-redcap with a Zenodo archive at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724; sensein/b2aiprep; sensein/senselab; eipm/bridge2ai-docs with a Zenodo archive at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; the Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles; and the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars programme. related_datasets adds doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 and doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84.
questions.quality_note: The 5-condition is met on both limbs: well above two distinct references, and a formal dataset citation that identifies the dataset by title and names both its authors and its publishing organisation rather than presenting a bare DOI.
questions.semantic_analysis: Scored using the permitted values of 0, 3 or 5 only. The references are genuinely distinct resources, not repeated links to one target, and two of them carry their own Zenodo DOIs, so the cross-linking is real rather than nominal. Each repository reference states its function and, for three of them, its licence (MIT, Apache-2.0), so a reuser can tell what each artefact does. One gap worth naming without deduction: no peer-reviewed article DOIs are cited, although source_caveats alludes to a feasibility publication and a white paper; under this question's stated criteria, non-publication external resources count as references and the formal dataset citation is present, so the top band is earned on its own terms.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition established from fields outside Q15, per the anti-circular rule: description (Q1/Q2) states 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada' on the basis of five named disease cohort categories; keywords (Q3) includes 'health'; collection_mechanisms (Q12) describes tablet-administered demographic surveys and validated questionnaires completed by participants in clinic.
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity, or subgroup details.
questions.score_label: Strong subgroup and at-risk characterisation, but no demographic distributions reported
questions.evidence: instances: 833 research participants, each carrying 'a clinician-assigned diagnostic label placing them in one of the disease cohort categories... or in the control group'. subpopulations gives two entries: demographic sub-populations 'identified by age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status in the demographics table', with distribution noting skews and that 'groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited'; and the five disease cohort groupings, noting 'The public data releases do not contain an equal distribution of these disease categories'. at_risk_populations documents cognitive impairment, dementia, psychiatric conditions and pediatric participants with comprehension-confirmed consent, guardian consent and assent_procedures. missing_data_documentation covers causes, patterns and handling. sampling_strategies records non-probability sampling, recruitment on 'the corresponding inclusion and exclusion criteria', and exclusion of participants who do not read or speak English.
questions.quality_note: Well above the 3-band of general human data without subgroup description: two distinct subpopulation axes are characterised, each with a qualitative distribution statement, and at-risk protections are detailed. Held at 4 because the top band asks for detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria, and neither is fully delivered.
questions.semantic_analysis: Two specific shortfalls drive the deduction. First, the demographic axes are named but no distribution is quantified anywhere: there are no counts or percentages by age, sex, gender, ethnicity or socioeconomic status, and the demographics table is described as existing rather than summarised, so a reuser cannot assess representativeness for their own question despite being told repeatedly that skews exist. Second, inclusion and exclusion criteria are referenced rather than enumerated - sampling_strategies points to 'the corresponding inclusion and exclusion criteria' without stating them, and only the English-fluency exclusion and the paediatric age range of 2 to 18 are given concretely. Against this, the qualitative characterisation is unusually thoughtful: the recruitment-trust and site-proximity mechanisms are named as causes of skew rather than skew being merely asserted, and the site-device-cohort confound recorded under known_biases is a real and non-obvious threat to subgroup comparability.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation.
questions.score_label: Pass - multiple persistent URLs and identifiers present
questions.evidence: page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; distribution_formats access_urls to the PhysioNet landing page and 'https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/'; external_resources URLs to https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, https://github.com/sensein/senselab, https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/, and Zenodo archives at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724 and https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep'.
questions.quality_note: Passes decisively. Persistent identifiers and resolvable URLs are present in quantity, and the landing page is version-specific so it resolves to the release this record describes.
questions.semantic_analysis: All URLs are well-formed and use plausible, correct domains for what they point to: physionet.org for the release, synapse.org with a syn-prefixed identifier for the controlled-access audio, zenodo.org for software archives, github.com for repositories. The DOI prefixes match their registrars throughout. Findability is further supported by archival flags set true on the two Zenodo-archived resources, which distinguishes archived from live references.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition established from fields outside this question's scoring core: page resolves to 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/', third_party_sharing.is_shared is true with distribution through PhysioNet and Synapse, and data_governance.access_review_process describes an operating request pathway.
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset (download, DUA, login).
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path with explicit access tier
questions.evidence: distribution_formats attaches access_urls to each format and states the gating explicitly: 'No direct download URL is published: the PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing and a signed data use agreement, so the access URL is the project landing page rather than a file endpoint', and for the audio 'access requires review by the Data Access Compliance Office and an institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement'. data_governance.access_review_process gives the full path: 'Registered access to the feature-only data requires registration on PhysioNet, confirmation of identity, and signature of the Bridge2AI-Voice Registered Access Agreement. Controlled access to raw audio requires completion of a Data Access Request Form and a Data Use Agreement, submission of the application to the Data Access Compliance Office for review and, upon approval, a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the applicant's institution.' raw_data_sources.access_details repeats the route and gives the Synapse URL and DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
questions.quality_note: The access tier is stated explicitly for each of the two tiers, the sequence of steps is given in order, the responsible office is named with a contact address, and the requirement for an institutional signatory is stated. A prospective user can determine exactly what they must do and who must sign.
questions.semantic_analysis: This is a case where an absent field is handled better than a populated one would be: download_url is not set, but rather than leaving that silently blank the record explains three times that no file endpoint exists because the files are credential-gated, and supplies the landing page as the correct substitute. That is an accurate description of PhysioNet credentialed access and avoids the common error of presenting a gated dataset as directly downloadable. The two tiers are also semantically justified rather than arbitrary, matching the re-identification risk analysis under participant_privacy: low-risk derived features at the registered tier, biometric raw audio at the controlled tier. The access terms are consistent with license_and_use_terms and with the prohibited_uses restriction on re-identification and participant contact.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License is clearly defined with explicit use guidance including intended uses, prohibited uses, discouraged uses, and comprehensive social impact analysis with risk identification and mitigation strategies.
questions.score_label: License + comprehensive use guidance + social impact analysis with mitigation strategies
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms as cited at Q9. intended_uses gives two use_category entries (research, cohort selection) with examples and usage_notes restricting use to 'Authorized Researchers who have been approved and have signed the applicable access agreement'. prohibited_uses gives five reasoned prohibitions covering re-identification, harm or stigmatisation to participants or communities, IP-based restriction of downstream access, sale of the data, and contacting data subjects without IRB approval and consent. discouraged_uses gives two entries covering hiring, insurance and surveillance applications, and uses that ignore the dataset's skews. future_use_impacts gives two entries: the multivariate skew warning framed as a risk of 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups', and the ELSI analysis covering 'risks of voice re-identification, vulnerabilities such as voice AI hacking, concerns around voice data sharing and privacy, and the influence of gender and racial diversity on the development and application of these technologies'. known_biases carry mitigation_strategy and known_limitations carry recommended_mitigation.
questions.quality_note: Every component of the top band is present and substantive. The prohibitions give reasons rather than bare rules, the discouraged uses name concrete misuse scenarios, and the social impact analysis addresses both distributional harm and modality-specific security risk.
questions.semantic_analysis: The use guidance is internally coherent with the rest of the record: the re-identification prohibition tracks the acknowledged residual risk under participant_privacy, and the prohibition on IP-based restriction is consistent with the non-obstruction clause in license_and_use_terms and with the Fort Lauderdale reference, so the same policy is expressed consistently in two places. Mitigation is genuinely attached rather than merely gestured at - remote collection, controlled recruitment variables and Spanish-language expansion against representation bias, and the recommendation to assess the multivariate distribution before use against the skew risk. The ELSI entry is notable for addressing voice-specific harms such as model hacking that a generic impact statement would miss. The one soft spot is that mitigation for the ELSI risks is implicit in the controlled-access model rather than stated as such, which was insufficient to move the score off the band given the strength of everything else.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Presence of version access, errata, update plans, source derivation, parent dataset linkages, missing data documentation, data split indicators, and provenance graph representation.
questions.score_label: Version history plus substantial textual processing lineage, short of a full provenance graph
questions.evidence: version_access, errata (three entries) and updates are all populated as cited at Q13. raw_data_sources gives two entries with source_description, source_type ('primary prospective collection', 'participant-reported and clinician-entered study records'), raw_data_format and access_details. missing_data_documentation covers causes, patterns and handling. splits states no recommended splits are provided. related_datasets records a typed 'is_new_version_of' link to doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. Processing lineage is given in preprocessing_strategies as an ordered chain from raw WAV through resampling, STFT, Mel and MFCC extraction, sparc articulatory estimation, openSMILE and Praat feature extraction, ppgs posteriorgrams, Whisper transcription and BIDS conversion, with sensein/b2aiprep named in external_resources as 'the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset, convert the raw audio waveforms into the Parquet feature files and merge the source data into the phenotype files'. Unpopulated: was_derived_from, parent_datasets.
questions.quality_note: Clearly above the 3-band, which is version history alone: entities, activities and agents are all identifiable in text, and the rubric expressly accepts textual provenance. Held below 5 because the derivation is narrated rather than expressed as linked provenance, so the lineage cannot be traversed programmatically.
questions.semantic_analysis: The elements of a W3C PROV-O style account are recoverable - entities are the raw waveforms, the phenotype exports and the derived feature tables; activities are the named transformation steps with their parameters; agents are b2aiprep as generating software, the clinicians as labelling agents and the research teams as collecting agents. What is missing is the typing: the single most important derivation edge in this dataset, that the released Parquet and TSV features were derived from the controlled-access raw audio, exists only as prose, while was_derived_from and parent_datasets sit empty and related_datasets types only the sibling and prior-version links. Data quality documentation is a real strength here and was weighed in favour of the score: the cleaning audit protocol, the disclosure that some audio files could not generate features and are absent from the bundled Parquet, the erratum recording broken Parquet files in version 3.0.0, and the anomalies entries on cross-site configuration drift together give an integrity picture that is unusually candid.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Metadata documents known biases using standardized taxonomies aligned with CROISSANT RAI standards, and includes fairness analysis.
questions.score_label: Taxonomy-categorised biases with fairness discussion, but no ontology mappings and partial mitigation
questions.evidence: known_biases gives four entries with BiasTypeEnum-style values: representation_bias ('collected at a limited number of geographic locations across five recording sites in the United States and Canada, and includes only fluent English speakers') with mitigation_strategy covering remote collection, controlled recruitment variables and Spanish expansion; selection_bias ('Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited'); measurement_bias ('different disease groups also had their data collected on different devices and under different collection configurations') with affected_subsets; and annotation_bias ('Diagnostic labels were assigned by a single labeler per instance, and the basis of the diagnosis varied by disorder'). future_use_impacts frames the skew risk as 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups'. known_limitations adds six typed entries and anomalies adds three.
questions.quality_note: Well above the 3-band of basic identification without taxonomy: the four bias types are drawn from a recognised enumeration and each carries a specific, mechanistic description rather than a generic caution. Held at 4 because the top band additionally requires standard taxonomy mappings and fairness analysis, and both are only partly delivered.
questions.semantic_analysis: The bias type assignments are semantically correct, which is the discriminating check - the site-device-cohort entanglement is properly classed as measurement bias rather than lumped under selection bias, and single-labeller diagnostic assignment is properly classed as annotation bias. The measurement_bias entry identifies a confound with real modelling consequences, since a classifier could learn recording configuration instead of pathology. Two shortfalls hold the score at 4. First, no AIO or CROISSANT RAI CURIEs are attached, so the categorisation is taxonomy-shaped in its vocabulary but not machine-mappable to an ontology, unlike the B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs the record uses elsewhere and could have paralleled. Second, fairness analysis is qualitative only: no subgroup counts, no distributional statistics and no subgroup performance considerations are given, so the repeatedly acknowledged skew cannot be quantified by a reuser, and mitigation_strategy is attached to only one of the four biases.

strengths: Ethics and privacy documentation is close to exemplary, covering IRB and REB review at three bodies, four consent modalities with a documented withdrawal rule, compensation with amounts and caps, and vulnerable-population safeguards including comprehension confirmation and an age threshold for assent.

Re-identification risk is analysed honestly and negatively, stating that k-anonymisation with k of 2 or more is not achieved and that voice re-identification cannot be excluded, and the two-tier access model is then justified by that analysis rather than asserted independently of it.

Governance and access are described end to end, from PhysioNet registration through the Registered Access Agreement to the DACO review and institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement, with a named office and contact address, so a prospective reuser can determine exactly what is required.

Identifier hygiene is high throughout: the version-specific DOI is used as the record's identity and the version-agnostic DOI is filed separately, registrar prefixes match their platforms across PhysioNet, Health Data Nexus and Zenodo, the NIH grant follows the expected pattern, and the RRID is well-formed and correctly scoped to the hosting resource.

Collection and preprocessing are documented to an operational level, naming recording hardware by model and generation, the division of labour between research staff and clinicians, and feature-extraction parameters specific enough to reproduce the pipeline structure.

Interoperability is strong on several axes at once: open standard formats, BIDS v1.9.0 conformance actually performed rather than merely declared, a resolvable LinkML schema URI, ICD-10 and FHIR alignments, and a documented participant_id join key linking feature files to phenotype tables.

source_caveats is used systematically to surface and adjudicate conflicts between sources on participant counts, enrolment targets, grant renderings, investigator name spellings and free-speech transcript inclusion, stating which source was preferred and why rather than silently choosing.

Negative and unflattering facts are disclosed rather than omitted, including unaudited Whisper transcripts, single-labeller diagnosis, broken Parquet files in a prior release, and the consortium's own sustainability self-score of 50 percent with named unmet criteria.
weaknesses: The collection timeframe is unresolved: 12 months is stated with no start or end date, and the record's own caveat records a conflicting four-year IRB study period, leaving reusers without a temporal anchor for the released data.

Machine-readable provenance is missing. was_derived_from and parent_datasets are empty, so the central derivation edge from raw audio to released features exists only as prose despite a complete narrative lineage being available.

Variable-level metadata is far thinner than the data it documents: four structural join and shape keys are recorded for a release whose phenotype tables span demographics, diagnosis, enrolment and questionnaires.

Software versions are largely unpinned. openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, sparc and ppgs carry no version and 'Whisper Large' names a model size rather than a checkpoint, so the feature-extraction pipeline is not exactly reproducible.

Demographic distributions are never quantified. Skew is acknowledged repeatedly but no counts or percentages by age, sex, gender, ethnicity or socioeconomic status are given, and per-cohort inclusion and exclusion criteria are referenced rather than enumerated.
Keywords are too few and too generic. Four broad terms, none naming a disease cohort or modality, leave the record hard to find for the conditions it actually covers.
Bias documentation uses taxonomy-shaped vocabulary without ontology mappings, offers no quantitative fairness analysis, and attaches a mitigation strategy to only one of the four biases recorded.

Several fields the rubric names are empty even though their substance appears elsewhere, notably publisher, data_protection_impacts and governance_committee_contact, which reduces machine readability without reducing human comprehension.
recommendations: Record explicit start and end dates for the collection window represented in version 3.1.0 and state whether the 12-month figure is a subset of the four-year study period, resolving the one failed consistency check.

Populate was_derived_from to type the derivation of the released Parquet and TSV features from the controlled-access raw audio, naming sensein/b2aiprep as the generating agent, which would move Q19 to the full provenance band.
Pin versions for openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, sparc and ppgs and name the exact Whisper checkpoint, so the documented extraction parameters become exactly reproducible.

Add demographic distribution summaries to subpopulations - counts or percentages by age, sex, gender, ethnicity and socioeconomic status, and per-cohort participant counts - and enumerate the per-cohort inclusion and exclusion criteria currently referenced only in the abstract.
Extend variables to cover the phenotype table columns, or reference the published JSON data dictionaries as the authoritative variable-level description.

Expand keywords to include the five disease cohort categories, the acoustic modalities and the released feature types, ideally with ICD-10 or MeSH terms matching the diagnostic labels already described in labeling_strategies.

Attach AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology identifiers to the four known_biases entries and add quantitative fairness context, and supply mitigation strategies for the selection, measurement and annotation biases as already done for representation bias.

Populate publisher with PhysioNet, consolidate the existing safeguard and breach-reporting material into an explicit data_protection_impacts entry, and set governance_committee_contact to the DACO address already recorded under data_governance.

Qualify is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present so that the absence of direct identifiers is not read as an absence of residual re-identification risk, given the acknowledged failure to reach k of 2.
